 Avishek Banerjee October 24, 2026, 15:56 IST / 2 min read ai hub Share Share ADVERTISEMENT
 The committee’s agenda spans capital market regulation, virtual digital assets, public debt, banking and tax reforms, while a separate parliamentary committee selects six subjects for reviewing the MPLADS scheme. Representational Image   Set Fortune India ✓ As Preferred on Google Proceed The Lok Sabha’s Standing Committee on Finance has selected 46 subjects for detailed examination during the 2026-27 financial year, covering artificial intelligence (AI) in finance, the performance of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), virtual digital assets and the management of public debt at the Centre and states.

According to Lok Sabha Bulletin Part-II dated October 23, 2026, the subjects relate to the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, NITI Aayog and the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. The agenda also includes reviews of government spending, financial sector regulation, taxation and the functioning of key public institutions.
 AI, Sebi and virtual digital assets on the agenda 
 The committee will examine emerging issues and prospects related to AI in finance and undertake a performance review of the International Financial Services Centre at GIFT City. It has also selected a study of virtual digital assets and the way forward.
 The review of Sebi will cover capital markets, alternative investment funds, venture capital and investor protection. Other subjects include financial sector regulation, investor protection, measures to prevent fraudulent practices and curb black money, and the Reserve Bank of India’s evolving role in the economy.

 The committee will also examine strategies for price and currency stability, currency management, and the impact of imports on foreign exchange reserves.
 Banking, insurance and tax reforms among 46 subjects 
 The banking and financial services agenda includes financial inclusion, emerging banking issues, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), pension sector regulation and payment and settlement systems. Health insurance will be examined in the context of universal coverage, affordability, claim settlement and policyholder protection.

 On taxation, the agenda covers indirect tax reforms, with emphasis on GST simplification, rationalisation and ease of compliance. Direct tax reforms, tax litigation and customs risk management are also included. Other subjects include long-term public finances and debt, small savings schemes, direct benefit transfers, special assistance to states for capital investment and monetisation of public sector assets.
 MPLADS committee selects six subjects 
 Separately, the Committee on Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) has selected six subjects for detailed examination in 2026-27.
 These include enhancement of MPLADS funds, guidelines governing their release, timely monitoring and execution of works, and the feasibility of convergence with the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) scheme. The committee will also examine the functioning of facilitation centres and technological hurdles in fund disbursement through the E-SAKSHI portal.
 To be sure, the bulletin sets out the subjects selected for examination during the year but does not provide findings or recommendations on them.
